holidays.name: National Take a Wild Guess Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to trusting your gut and making a bold guess about anything, from trivia answers to what's in the mystery casserole at the office potluck. Accuracy is optional, confidence is mandatory.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, humorous observance listed in quirky holiday calendars. It has no single documented founder, and it spread through novelty-day lists and social media.
holidays.funFact: Guessing under uncertainty is a real field of study, and research shows people's quick gut estimates are often surprisingly close, especially when averaged across a crowd.

holidays.name: National Banana Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the world's most popular fruit, celebrated with banana bread, banana splits, smoothies, and peeling with unearned swagger.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance popularized by food-holiday calendars. Bananas have been traded globally since the late 1800s, when refrigerated shipping made them a household staple.
holidays.funFact: Bananas are technically berries, while strawberries are not. The bananas in stores are mostly one variety, the Cavendish, and they are genetically near-identical clones.

holidays.name: National Glazed Spiral Ham Day
holidays.description: A salute to the sweet, sticky, pre-sliced holiday centerpiece that makes carving effortless and leftovers endless.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance that falls around Easter season in many years, when spiral ham is a traditional table star. Spiral slicing was patented in the 1940s by Harry Hoenselaar, who started the HoneyBaked Ham company.
holidays.funFact: Harry Hoenselaar invented a spiral ham slicing machine and opened his first HoneyBaked Ham store in Detroit in 1957.

holidays.name: World Art Day
holidays.description: An international celebration of creativity, painting, sculpting, doodling, and all the ways humans make things beautiful. It encourages everyone to pick up a pencil and make something, however questionable.
holidays.origin: Recognized by UNESCO, which in 2019 proclaimed April 15 as World Art Day to promote art and its contribution to sustainable development. The date honors the birthday of Leonardo da Vinci, born April 15, 1452.
holidays.funFact: Leonardo da Vinci wrote his notebooks in mirror-image script, and he left behind fewer than 20 confirmed paintings despite being one of history's most famous artists.

holidays.name: Rubber Eraser Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the humble eraser, the unsung hero of every mistake ever made in pencil. Celebrate by correcting your errors and enjoying the satisfying crumbly shavings.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance said to honor the invention of the rubber eraser. In 1770, English engineer Edward Nairne reportedly sold the first rubber erasers after discovering that rubber could rub out pencil marks.
holidays.funFact: Before rubber erasers, people commonly used bread crumbs to rub out pencil and charcoal marks.
